rules.summary: The build uses a module the policy denies
rules.explanation: The dependency policy names this module as forbidden. Remove it or use the replacement the policy names.

rules.summary: A direct dependency is not on the allowed list
rules.explanation: The dependency policy lists the only modules the organisation approved. Ask for the module to be approved or use an approved one.

rules.summary: A repository is not on the allowed list
rules.explanation: Dependencies may only come from the repositories the policy names. Every further repository is a further place a module can be replaced.

rules.summary: A repository is reached without TLS
rules.explanation: allowInsecureProtocol lets anyone on the network path replace what the build downloads.

rules.summary: The build resolves from the local Maven repository
rules.explanation: Anything installed on the machine, by any build, can replace a dependency in mavenLocal(). Resolve from it only in a local workflow and filter its content.

rules.summary: A dependency is declared with a dynamic version
rules.explanation: A version such as 1.+, latest.release or a range picks up whatever is published next, including a malicious or breaking release.
A snapshot changes under the same version, so the build cannot be reproduced and the content cannot be verified.

rules.summary: A test library is on a production class path
rules.explanation: Test libraries ship code that has no place in production, and they widen what an attacker can reach. Declare them for tests only.

rules.summary: A module is forced to a version
rules.explanation: force overrides every other request and outlives the reason it was added. Accept it with an ignore rule that names the reason and expires.
Without a lock file the next resolution can pick other versions than the last one, unnoticed. Kreate's dependencyLocking writes one.
In Gradle's default lock mode a deleted lock file goes unnoticed. LockMode.STRICT fails instead.
Without gradle/verification-metadata.xml, or with verification set to lenient or off, a replaced artifact is not noticed.

rules.summary: The Gradle distribution is not checked
rules.explanation: gradle-wrapper.properties names no distributionSha256Sum, so a replaced distribution runs with the rights of every build.

rules.summary: The Gradle distribution is downloaded without TLS
rules.explanation: An http distributionUrl lets anyone on the network path replace the build tool itself.

rules.summary: A dependency is several major releases behind
rules.explanation: Every skipped breaking release makes the upgrade harder and leaves fixes behind.

rules.summary: The dependencies are too far behind in total
rules.explanation: Libyears add up how far each direct dependency lags behind its latest release. The total exceeds what the policy allows.
